ai_show_review.summary: Fiery Viola Lee Blues and tight Alligator>Caution in historic Monterey slot
ai_show_review.blurb: The short Monterey Pop set delivers a scorching Viola Lee Blues and an adventurous Alligator > Caution transition. Jerry's lead work is electric, while Pigpen adds gritty organ on Caution. Overall the performance is high‑octane despite modest recording quirks.
ai_show_review.review:
June 18, 1967 at the Monterey Fairgrounds captures the Grateful Dead’s first major festival appearance in a blistering four‑song burst. The band launches with a ferocious Viola Lee Blues that showcases Jerry Garcia’s searing guitar tone, even if some of the early soundboard sources are a touch muddy. After a crisp rendition of Cold Rain And Snow, they dive into an experimental Alligator that segues straight into Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks), where Pigpen’s organ swells over a driving rhythm section. The energy never wanes, and despite a few technical hiccups in some recordings, the set remains a vivid snapshot of the Dead’s early blues‑rock vigor.

From a listening standpoint the cleanest capture comes from the Kaplan soundboard tape (gd1967-06-18.115858.sbd.kaplan.flac16), which preserves the band’s dynamics without the interview bleed or dropouts found elsewhere. This version lets listeners hear the raw power of Jerry’s improvisations, Phil’s steady bass foundation, and Bill Kreutzmann’s propulsive drumming, making it the most enjoyable way to experience this historic moment.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard clarity with no major dropouts, preserving the full energy of the set.

key_highlights: Scorching Viola Lee Blues with Jerry’s blazing lead work
Alligator > Caution sequence that pushes early experimentation
Pigpen’s gritty organ texture on Caution adds depth
Historic Monterey Pop Festival debut, a snapshot of the band’s early sound

band_performance.Jerry: Electric guitar throughout; fiery leads on Viola Lee Blues and Alligator, though a few recordings note mild muddiness.
band_performance.Bob: Provides solid rhythm‑guitar support that locks in with the band’s drive.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ shines on Caution, adding a gritty texture; harmonica moments are uneven due to mic issues.
band_performance.Billy: Keeps a tight, propulsive beat that underpins the high‑octane set.
